map.name: script
map.gives: one JSON line on standard output
map.story:
Example: `python sample.py` with no arguments reports on sample.py itself.
The path comes from `sys.argv[1]` only when an argument is present. Otherwise the script uses `__file__`, its own source file.
map.text: script — reads a file path from the command line, reports on it, and writes the result as JSON to standard output

children.text:
Bring in the two standard modules the script needs:
json — to write the result as a JSON line
sys — to read the command-line arguments

out = the result dict from report(), which reads one file, counts the digits in it, prints a summary line, and returns the numbers
The path is the first command-line argument when the caller gives one, and the script's own file when the caller gives none.
Print the result dict as one JSON line, so another program can read the output.

map.name: Tally
map.gives: a new tally with its own total
map.text: Tally() -> a tally object — makes a counter that keeps one running total for its caller

map.name: Tally.__init__
map.gives: nothing; the object now has total 0
map.text: __init__(self) -> None — starts a new Tally with an empty running total

children.text:
total = the running sum the Tally builds up, set to 0 at the start
Every new Tally begins from zero, so add() has a number to grow.

map.name: Tally.add
map.story:
Example: after t.add(3) on a fresh Tally, t.total is 6, not 3.
Every number counts double.
map.text: add(self, n) -> None — adds n twice over to the running total

children.text: take a number n and add double its value to self.total

map.name: digits
map.gives: the digit values, in the order they appear
map.text: digits(text) -> list of ints — pulls every digit character out of the text and returns it as a number

children.text: out = the digit values found so far, empty at the start
look at each character of text in turn, and when the character is a digit, store it as a number, not as a character
give the collected numbers back to the caller

map.name: spread
map.gives: the distance from the smallest to the largest
map.text: spread(nums) -> number — measures how far apart the largest and smallest values in nums are

children.text:
top = the largest value in nums
low = the smallest value in nums
give back the gap between them, top minus low

map.name: report
map.gives: a dict of file, count, total and spread
map.story:
Example: a file holding "a3b4" gives count 2, total 14, spread 1, and prints "2 digits, doubled total 14, spread 1".
total is not the sum of the digits: Tally.add doubles each number.
A file with no digits returns early with only file and count, so the caller sees a dict without total or spread.
map.text: report(path) -> a result dict — reads one file, counts the digits in it, prints a summary line, and returns the numbers

children.text: src = the whole text of the file at path, read as UTF-8
nums = every digit in that text as a number, from digits()

when the file holds no digits, stop here and give back only the path and a count of 0
the later steps need at least one number, so this branch protects them

t = a new Tally, from Tally(), and each number in nums goes into it with t.add
t.total is therefore twice the sum of the digits, because add doubles what it takes
wide = the distance from the smallest digit to the largest, from spread()
line = one sentence with the digit count, the doubled total and the spread, and print puts it on screen for the person who runs this
give the caller the same three measures with the file path, as a dict
